Bay-Bakool Low Potential Agropastoral regional centre under long-term Al-Shabaab siege, supplied largely by air, with a regional hospital but highly restricted rural access. Exit probability reflects moderate CMAM/health coverage, only sporadically or partially accessible (garrison town/road blockades) programme access and high endemic disease pressure; incidence reflects the livelihood vulnerability, structural IDP hosting and conflict constraints on livelihoods. Month-to-month variability is driven by pronounced lean-season swings, recurrent drought/flood shocks, volatile displacement flows, unstable conflict and access and unstable market supply and prices. Structural information is thin, so priors are widened rather than shifted.
